dish: Handmade 100% yellowtail fishball noodles (mee pok / kolo mee)
address: 77 Circuit Road, #01-450, MacPherson, Singapore 370077
w: Young hawkerpreneur Douglas Ng rebuilt his grandmother's recipe into a hawker-fame story — soft, bouncy fishballs made from pure yellowtail with no added flour that won a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2016; after stints at Golden Mile and Timbre+, the stall settled at Blk 77 Circuit Road in MacPherson.

dish: Crab bee hoon in intensely sweet crab-and-seafood broth
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-29, 79A Circuit Road, Singapore 371079
w: Opened by former local actor Huang Yiliang, this humble evening-only stall cooks each bowl of crab bee hoon to order, drawing out a deeply sweet seafood broth — with a steamed fish and homemade omelette that regulars rate just as highly. A cult name of the renovated Circuit Road hawker centre.

dish: Old-school wok-fried Hokkien prawn mee
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-10, 79A Circuit Road, Singapore 371079
w: An old-school Hokkien mee (from S$4) simmered and fried in prawn-head and pork stock with egg, prawn, pork and yellow noodles, then left to stew so the strands soak up the umami — a repeatedly-listed Circuit Road favourite the food blogs queue for.

dish: Mock-meat vegetarian satay (~S$1/stick) & otah
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-92, 79A Circuit Road, Singapore 371079
w: Victor's vegetarian satay — grilled mock-meat skewers at around S$1 a stick — draws long lines from residents and non-vegetarians alike, alongside otah and a spread of meat-free hawker classics that regularly headline Circuit Road stall guides.

dish: Less-oil char kway teow (soft-boiled egg or omelette)
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-19, 79 Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: The uncle who dances to instrumental music as he fries — his char kway teow is cooked with less oil than most and can be topped with a soft-boiled egg or omelette (about S$5), a Circuit Road performance-and-plate that the SPH food titles keep naming.

dish: 24-hour prata (crispy-yet-doughy) & mutton nasi biryani
address: 538 MacPherson Road, Singapore 368222
w: A family-run 24-hour Indian-Muslim diner on MacPherson Road since 1998 and a go-to supper spot — famed for prata that comes out crispy on the outside yet slightly doughy within, plus a well-loved mutton nasi biryani (~S$7) and proper mutton soup for the night-shift crowd.

dish: Claypot rice — smoked duck, char siew, pig trotter, bak kut teh
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: A claypot specialist whose range runs from smoked-duck rice and barbecue-pork rice to pig trotters and bak kut teh, with a classic claypot chicken rice around S$7 — a hearty Circuit Road standby featured across the SPH stall round-ups.

dish: Chicken & mutton briyani (compact two-dish menu)
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-14, 79 Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: A family-run briyani stall with a deliberately tiny menu — just chicken briyani and mutton briyani, both under S$7 — plating generous, flavourful helpings that make it one of the Circuit Road names the food titles single out.

dish: Fried oyster / oyster omelette & fried carrot cake
address: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
w: A third-generation hawker cooking fried oyster, orh luak (oyster omelette) and fried carrot cake from a family recipe handed down by his grandfather — an old-school Circuit Road wok stall the SPH lifestyle titles both flag.

dish: Prawn noodles in 8-hour prawn-and-pork-rib broth
address: 1 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347834
w: A Potong Pasir prawn-noodle institution first established in 1971 and now second-generation, named for the ancestral province of founder Png Kim Soon. The broth is built from fried prawn shells and pork ribs simmered eight hours, served across a sprawling 20-dish menu of prawn, pork rib, intestine, baby abalone and clam combinations.

dish: Bak chor mee with pork liver (Tai Thong)
address: Sin Keng Seng Eating House, 47 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347867
w: Opened by an apprentice of a famous bak chor mee master, this Tai Thong Crescent coffeeshop stall turns out an old-school minced-pork noodle — vinegary, lard-slicked, with fresh pork liver — that veteran hawker bloggers rank among the area's best.

dish: Seremban-style cuttlefish bee hoon (lai fen) & pork curry
address: The Commerze @ Irving, 1 Irving Place, Singapore 369546
w: An ex-Hyatt manager's stall cooking authentic Seremban, Malaysia dishes — springy cuttlefish bee hoon (lai fen) with sweet sauce and a rich pork curry. After its beloved hole-in-the-wall Potong Pasir Ave 3 coffeeshop closed in March 2024, it reopened bigger and air-conditioned at The Commerze @ Irving in Sept 2024, on the MacPherson/Tai Seng edge.

dish: Third-generation Shangri-La Confectionery bakes & cafe fare
address: 148 Potong Pasir Avenue 1, #01-37, Singapore 350148
w: Run by the third generation behind the old Shangri-La Confectionery & Delicatessen, Kizuna is the family's Potong Pasir revamp from heritage bakery into a neighbourhood cafe — keeping the old-school bakes while adding brunch plates and coffee.

dish: Brown-butter waffles, cakes & gelato
address: 51 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-59 Poiz Centre, Singapore 347697
w: A vibrant salmon-pink cafe tucked into Poiz Centre, known for crisp brown-butter waffles, cakes and gelato and inventive drinks (Grape Yakult Honey Sencha) — Eatbook scored it 7.5/10 and it's become a study-and-brunch favourite of the estate.

dish: Duck confit on mashed potato with homemade sauce
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-30, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: ITE culinary grads Darryl and Shi Long bring affordable European dining to a hawker stall — their best-selling duck confit (S$12) is a fork-tender leg on fluffy mash in a moat of rich house sauce, plus truffle pasta — a headline act of the new Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre.

dish: Kway chap with braised pork belly & offal (from S$5)
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: A legendary kway chap name dating to the 1980s, now with a Woodleigh Village outlet — a set from S$5 gets broad rice sheets in braised gravy with expertly done pork belly, big and small intestine, tau pok and more.

dish: Henghua-style white lor mee with seafood & pork
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-27, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: A rare Henghua (Putian)-style white lor mee — a velvety, savoury (not dark) broth loaded with seafood, pork and vegetables — one of the standout regional-Chinese stalls the food guides pick out at Woodleigh Village.

dish: Crispy-skin fried chicken wings
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-18, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: An outlet of the famed fried-chicken-wing name some rate the best in Singapore — light, crackly skin over juicy meat — one of the established brands that anchored the new Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre when it opened in Sept 2024.

dish: Meat-free 'char siew' kolo mee, fish bee hoon & kway chap
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-13, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: The hawker centre's sole vegetarian stall, run by Darryl Tong, plating a menu that reads nothing like a typical meat-free spread — 'char siew' kolo mee, fried fish bee hoon and kway chap done entirely vegan.

dish: Nasi kerabu (blue pea rice) with fried chicken
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: Fragrant Kelantanese-style nasi kerabu — gorgeous blue-pea rice (S$7.80) with herbs and a crisp, juicy fried chicken leg — one of the young-hawker Malay stalls the food guides highlight at Woodleigh Village.

dish: Smooth Cantonese-style congee
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-35, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: A specialist in authentic Cantonese porridge — silky, slow-simmered congee — among the quieter but well-regarded stalls the food bloggers pick out at the new Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre.

dish: Mexican rice bowls & tacos
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: A Mexican stall bringing hearty rice bowls and tacos to hawker prices — part of the wave of young, cross-cuisine entrepreneurs that made Woodleigh Village one of Singapore's most internationally varied hawker centres.

dish: Hong Kong egglet (eggette) with ice cream
address: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-40, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
w: Crisp-shelled HK-style egglets (gai daan jai) served as ice-cream sandwiches and waffles — the sweet-treat stall that both major food guides call out by name at Woodleigh Village.

dish: Specialty coffee from a national barista champion
address: The Woodleigh Mall, #01-55, 11 Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore 367803
w: A cosy Bidadari cafe from the team of a Singapore National Barista Champion — carefully pulled specialty coffee alongside cafe fare like avocado toast and shakshuka, a draw for the estate's brunch crowd.

dish: Fried-chicken pancake stacks & all-day brunch
address: The Woodleigh Mall, 11 Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore 367803
w: A train-themed, pet-friendly outpost of the Australian grocer-cafe, with a cabin-style seating nook and signature pancake stacks (the Fried Chicken Stack pairs Pancake Parlour pancakes with buttermilk fried chicken and chilli honey) — a headline brunch anchor of the Bidadari mall.
